# Notes for a rexafs Larix reader

These notes describe the generated fixtures and the inspected xraylarch
2026.3.1 implementation. They are not a complete specification of every object
that a Larch session can store. The
[official overview](https://xraypy.github.io/xraylarch/data.html#saving-and-loading-larch-session-files-larix-files)
explains the distinction between reading a session and loading it into an
analysis environment.

## Container and symbols

The [writer and reader](https://github.com/xraypy/xraylarch/blob/2026.3.1/larch/io/save_restore.py)
use a gzip-compressed UTF-8 stream. The decompressed first line starts with
`##LARIX: 1.0`. The remainder is sectioned text, not one JSON document:

```text
##LARIX: 1.0      Larch Session File
##Date Saved: ...
##<CONFIG>
##Python Version: ...
...
##</CONFIG>
##<Session Commands>
...history text...
##</Session Commands>
##<Symbols: count=...>
<:_xasgroups:>
{"__class__": "Dict", "display name": "group_symbol"}
<:group_symbol:>
{"__class__": "Group", ...}
##</Symbols>
```

Each symbol has a marker line and one JSON-style value on the following line.
Larch uses Python's permissive JSON encoding: `NaN`, `Infinity` and `-Infinity`
can appear as unquoted tokens. The typed metadata fixture contains them in
lmfit parameter defaults and bounds, while its absorption arrays remain finite.
A strict JSON parser will need an explicit policy for these metadata values;
do not reject an otherwise usable spectrum or substitute finite numbers
silently. In `expected.json`, nonfinite scalar observations use string spellings.
The optional `_xasgroups` dictionary maps display names to symbol names.
With `auto_xasgroups=True`, this writer adds the index but reports the original
symbol-list length in `count`; valid fixtures therefore contain one extra
symbol beyond that count. Preserve this compatibility case. Section endings
and successful payload decoding are stronger completion checks than that count.

History and configuration are provenance. Preserve history as text. Reading
the fixtures must not execute it or treat source paths as files to reopen.
Inspecting unknown saved objects as metadata is sufficient for absorption
import; reconstructing arbitrary Python classes is outside that task.

## Array encodings

[jsonutils.py](https://github.com/xraypy/xraylarch/blob/2026.3.1/larch/utils/jsonutils.py)
tags Groups, dictionaries, lists, tuples, Journals, parameters and arrays with
`__class__`. The current array representation has two JSON layers:

```json
{"__class__":"b64ndarray","__value__":"{\"_type_\":\"b64ndarray\",\"shape\":[2],\"dtype\":\"<f8\",\"value\":\"...\"}"}
```

Decode the string in `__value__` as JSON.
[npjson.py](https://github.com/xraypy/xraylarch/blob/2026.3.1/larch/utils/npjson.py)
defines the inner shape, NumPy dtype descriptor, and base64-encoded C-order
bytes. There is no `.npy` header. Validate the shape product, element width,
byte order and decoded byte length. Complex values interleave real and imaginary
components. The metadata fixture also includes a big-endian float64 vector,
float32 matrix, int64 vector, Boolean vector, and empty `(0, 3)` array.

The legacy fixture sets the writer's existing `USE_NPJSON=False` switch. It
uses `{"__class__":"Array", "__shape__":[...], "__dtype__":"float64",
"value":[...]}`. Complex legacy arrays store separate flattened real and
imaginary lists. This is a compatibility encoding generated by the pinned
writer, not a claim that the file was produced by an older application release.

## Absorption import and saved processing

For the supplied XAS groups, `energy` is in eV and `mu` is the already selected
dimensionless absorption signal. Detector arrays, two-dimensional source
tables, metadata, and saved processing arrays should remain available without
replacing these values. `xdat`/`ydat` alone do not prove that a group contains
X-ray absorption; the `non-xas` fixture demonstrates a position scan.

`norm`, `flat` and `bkg` have the energy grid's length. `k` and `chi` use a
different grid, and `r` and complex `chir` use a third grid. Each analyzed
fixture has 241 k points and 326 R points. Keep complex values and independent
shapes. `callargs`, `pre_edge_details`, `autobk_details` and Journals are saved
settings and provenance; importing them does not establish that rexafs has
reproduced Larch's calculations. Repeated Journal keys and group order matter.

The typed metadata fixture's parameter expression is an ordinary numerical
constraint, `2 * amplitude`. A reader can retain its text and stored value.
The synthetic four-point spectrum exercises serialization only and is too
short for the real-data processing recipe.

The bundle does not cover full FEFF fitting sessions, fitted model objects,
PCA/linear-combination results, external HDF5 handles, old `save_groups()` files,
or every historical Larch version. The original measurements, both array
encodings, all numeric expectations and validation tooling are supplied so
format support can be extended without changing the existing fixtures.
